title: Fundamental Reality
definition: The true nature of the universe as a unified, participatory phenomenon, which is experienced directly and can be understood through ceasing manipulation of perception.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine looking at a scene without trying to interpret it or assign meanings to objects. Just seeing what's there. That's a glimpse of fundamental reality.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Fundamental reality is the raw, uncollapsed field of experience. It's what remains when we stop the cognitive machinery of separation, such as subject/object or this/that.
difficulty_levels.expert: Fundamental reality is the recognition that the universe is a unified, inseparable phenomenon. It challenges the scientific understanding of reality as discrete particles and waves, and instead suggests a participatory, interconnected universe. This concept has philosophical implications and connects to other fields, such as quantum physics and Eastern philosophy.

extra_fields.insight: Fundamental reality can be experienced directly and is a participatory, unified phenomenon.
